title: Publish updated pricing guidance for AEs (Hosted API meters, free tier/overage, retries/caching) + FAQ
creator: Chris Osei
description:
Goal
Publish an updated, customer-ready-but-internal Sales Enablement package for AEs that explains Hosted API pricing/metering clearly and consistently post-meter hardening work.

This ticket covers:
1) Sales Enablement FAQ (Confluence) + objection handling (scripted responses)
2) Internal pricing guidance page(s) that map meters -> packaging (free tier, overage, credits) and provide guardrails for quoting/discounting
3) Rollout plan with RevOps (training, links in enablement hub, versioning, and “what changed” summary)

Why now
We’re in the middle of meter hardening (token counting alignment, retries/idempotency, cache-hit attribution, streaming semantics). Sales is getting repeated questions about fairness and invoice/usage-export alignment, and Legal is seeing more usage-definition redlines. We need a single approved source for AEs that is consistent with:
- Finance/RevRec source-of-truth meters and invoice mapping
- Legal clause library for usage-based pricing definitions
- Product packaging experiments (avoid mixing experimental behavior with GA guidance)

Primary deliverable links (drafts)
- Confluence (Sales Enablement): Hosted API pricing FAQ + objection handling
  sources/confluence/sales-enablement/pricing-guidance/hosted-api-pricing-faq-and-objection-handling.json
- Confluence (Product Docs): Hosted API packages: free tier + overage policy
  sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json
- Confluence (Legal): Usage-based pricing legal terms playbook
  sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/usage-based-pricing-legal-terms-playbook.json
- Public-ish docs PR (for consistency checks only; do not promise timelines externally)
  sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-642-update-usage-and-billing-faq.json

Scope (what this ticket MUST cover)
- Definitions AEs can rely on in customer conversations:
  - “Billed tokens” vs “raw tokens” and why they may differ (e.g., caching and server-side retries/fallback prevention)
  - Retry behavior and idempotency (what we bill for; what we don’t; how to avoid double charging)
  - Streaming semantics (partial chunks, disconnects, completion accounting)
  - Cache-hit attribution (when cache reduces billed tokens vs when it doesn’t; customer-visible fields)
  - Usage API vs invoice: expected lags, timezone/day-boundary conventions, and dispute workflow
- Free tier and overage:
  - Included usage definition and how it’s counted
  - What happens at limit (soft cap vs hard stop; rate limiting; notifications)
  - Guidance for “trial extensions” and credits (what Sales can offer vs requires approval)
- Experiment / pricing-variant hygiene:
  - AEs should not mix experimental plan details into standard guidance
  - How to confirm cohort exposure (RevOps-owned CRM fields)

Out of scope
- Changing pricing, creating new discount programs, or committing to retroactive invoice adjustments
- Writing contract language from scratch (we will reference Legal’s playbook and clause library; Legal owns final language)

Stakeholders / reviewers
- Product: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API PM), Chris Osei (Product Ops)
- Sales: Jordan Blake (CRO) for final enablement approval; one pilot AE group for feedback
- Legal: Sofia Mendes (commercial counsel) for wording approval
- Finance/RevRec: Emily Stone (RevRec) for meter/invoice alignment
- RevOps: (via INT-945 / internal request) for distribution + CRM references

Acceptance criteria
- Confluence page(s) published with:
  - Clear, unambiguous definitions for tokens/requests/retries/caching/streaming (no “hand-wavy” language)
  - Explicit disclaimers where behavior can vary (e.g., region/model/version) and where customers should look (Usage API fields)
  - Standard AE talk track + “what to say / what not to say” callouts
  - Linkouts to: meter spec, legal playbook, free-tier policy, dispute process, and the current usage API fields
- Legal sign-off recorded (link to INT-962) and a changelog section added
- RevOps rollout completed:
  - Linked in sales enablement hub
  - Announced in #sales and #solutions-engineering
  - 15-min enablement walkthrough scheduled + recording posted
- Versioning: page header includes “Effective date” and “Last reviewed” and points to prior version

Open questions
- Final customer-facing phrasing for cache-hit attribution: does Legal prefer “may reduce billed tokens” vs “reduces billed tokens when eligible” language?
- Can we safely mention the new usage API fields (“billed_tokens”, “cache_hit”) as GA, or is it still staged? (Need Eng confirmation tied to PR-27485 + SDK rollouts)
- Dispute window: ensure we mirror standard MSA/Order Form language and don’t create new commitments

Proposed structure (Sales Enablement page)
1) TL;DR: How Redwood bills Hosted API usage
2) Token counting: billed vs raw, prompt vs completion, tool calls
3) Retries/fallbacks/idempotency
4) Streaming
5) Caching
6) Why invoice ≠ real-time dashboard (freshness + timezone)
7) Free tier, overage, and credits
8) Objections (copy/paste answers)
9) Escalation paths (Support + Finance + Legal)

Rollout checklist
- Draft reviewed by: Nikhil (Product), Emily (RevRec), Sofia (Legal)
- Pilot with 3 AEs + 2 SEs: collect feedback, update confusing sections
- Publish + announce + training
- Add link to onboarding checklist for new AEs

References / related work
- Meter changes / hardening:
  - PR-27463 fix double-counting on stream retry
  - PR-27485 expose cache-hit + billed token fields in usage API
  - PR-511 align token counting w/ OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- Meter change control: PM-1872
- Free tier copy finalization: PM-1865

Risks
- If guidance is published before meter semantics stabilize, we’ll create rework and increase legal/sales confusion. Mitigation: include effective date + explicit “current behavior” bullets and update notes; coordinate publish timing with shadow-billing results.

Next step
Lock “approved wording” blocks with Legal/RevRec, then publish to Confluence and proceed with enablement rollout.
comments: 2026-02-12 (Chris Osei): Created. Sales keeps asking for a canonical explanation of billed vs raw tokens + caching/retries. Let’s consolidate into one AE-ready page and get Legal sign-off. Elliot to own doc polish + publication; Nikhil to provide technical accuracy; Emily/Sofia to approve language.

2026-02-13 (Elliot Price): Draft outline in Confluence created; pulled in sections from the older FAQ and added new headings for caching + streaming. Flagged two areas needing Legal wording: (1) cache-hit attribution promises, (2) dispute window language. Linked INT-962 for formal sign-off.

2026-02-14 (Nikhil Sharma): Added technical notes: tool-call tokens should be described as part of completion tokens (and billed tokens) when generated by the model. Also added explicit guidance to ask customers to use idempotency keys to avoid client retry duplicates. Still need Eng to confirm GA timing on billed_tokens/cache_hit in Usage API.

2026-02-17 (Emily Stone): Finance review: avoid any language implying we’ll retroactively change invoices. Add a line: ‘If there’s a suspected discrepancy, Redwood will investigate and may issue credits per policy.’ Also add timezone/freshness caveat for daily exports; align with month-end freeze window process.

2026-02-18 (Sofia Mendes): Legal notes: keep definitions consistent with clause library. Use ‘Billed Tokens’ as the defined term; avoid ‘fair’/‘unfair’ framing; do not state caching ‘always’ reduces bill—use ‘may’ + ‘when eligible’. Dispute section should reference the contract dispute window, not set a new timeline in enablement docs.

2026-02-20 (Jordan Blake): Please add a short ‘What to say / what not to say’ box for AEs. Especially around retries: we should say ‘we have safeguards to prevent double-counting server-side retries’ but not promise ‘never’. Also include an escalation channel for deals that require audit logs/retention assurances (route to Legal + Security).

2026-02-24 (Elliot Price): Updated the draft with Legal/Finance edits and added a ‘Changelog’ + ‘Effective date’ block. Next: confirm usage API fields rollout status (PR-27485 + SDK PRs) and schedule the 15-min enablement session with RevOps. Target publish early next week pending final sign-off.
